subject.title: Agent loop allows simulated tool calls instead of enforcing real tool invocation

question: Should internal OpenClaw agent turns add strict enforcement for clear tool-required requests, and should that behavior be default or opt-in per agent/model/provider?
rationale: Current source intentionally mixes warning-only diagnostics, bounded text-tool promotion, and Gateway-only `tool_choice` enforcement, so the remaining fix changes both a security boundary and local-model compatibility behavior.

options.title: Design opt-in strict enforcement
options.body: Add a bounded strict mode or policy contract for explicitly tool-required internal turns while preserving current compatibility defaults until maintainers approve a broader default change.

options.title: Make strict enforcement default
options.body: Treat clear internal tool-required text-only turns as failures across agent runs, accepting upgrade and local-model compatibility risk as a security default change.

options.title: Fold into response-gate design
options.body: Defer this issue to the broader final-response and ledger-verification design so simulated tool calls and unsupported success claims share one policy model.

recommendation.title: Design opt-in strict enforcement
recommendation.body: Add a bounded strict mode or policy contract for explicitly tool-required internal turns while preserving current compatibility defaults until maintainers approve a broader default change.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining question is a security/default policy decision in the agent runtime, and steipete has the strongest current related review and source-history signal.
